Sampled HR@10 measures performance within the sampled candidate set; it can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation, even in expectation. Preserve the pinned 99-negative evaluator and interpret results specifically for that benchmark. Fixed users, candidates and seeds make comparisons reproducible but do not remove sampling bias. [Krichene and Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

For uncertainty, a practical adaptation of paired bootstrap is to retain each model’s per-user hit indicator, resample users with replacement within each category using identical indices for both models, then compute the difference between their equally weighted four-category means. Report the observed macro difference, its bootstrap interval and category-level differences. This preserves pairing and dataset weights without changing the evaluator. Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the trained models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed and negative-sampling variability. [Paired bootstrap methodology](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/)

Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit finite validation data; the winning validation score becomes optimistic, and ordinary pairwise bootstrap intervals do not correct this adaptive selection. Practical search controls: predeclare the trial budget and selection rule, log every attempted configuration, limit repeated tuning around tiny gains, and reserve held-out evaluation for the final selected model. Under the required fixed splits and seeds, treat validation intervals as descriptive diagnostics rather than selection-adjusted evidence of generalization. [Cawley and Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
